thread.en: To be honest, the cyberbullying in the LPL this year is way more vicious than ever before. BLG's international results this year have actually been quite solid, including MSI—even though they lost the final, look at how brilliantly they played against T1 and in the winners' bracket finals. Just because of the MSI and EWC setbacks people keep flaming Bin, non-stop. Who the hell could take that?

top.en: Let me say something controversial. This year, the LPL has been mocking Valorant for all four teams going out in the top 16, but many haven't realized that almost all of our international results in recent years were carried by BLG. Yet, BLG gets flamed daily in China, especially Bin, who gets the worst of it. He used to be able to handle it, but after MSI, he couldn't take it anymore and changed his playstyle, or rather, his mentality just shattered. And honestly, apart from his K'Sante getting ganked in game 4, calling him the war criminal at MSI makes no sense. The bot lane and jungler were not clean at all. BLG is essentially carried by their mid and top. You could see that against WE; without them, they wouldn't even have made MSI, let alone earned the 4th seed. Now, I feel like Bin doesn't even know how to play his old style in the top lane anymore. If Knight can't step up, they'll be lucky to reach the quarterfinals. The most disgusting thing about the LPL is that people know which team will actually get results, yet they flame them every day. If you show any confidence and make a mistake, you get cyberbullied. And the player you're bullying is the core of the team. The funniest part is that people still use this team's recent results, the last bit of LPL's face, to mock other games. Casters and viewers are all the same. When [~0:Master] came this year, a caster boldly claimed BLG was invincible, but now, if it were Master, they wouldn't even be able to fight back. In short, looking at this year, the LPL's chances of winning Worlds are slim, but the viewers and some casters don't seem to care. They just want to bully people online and feel good about themselves. Results don't matter. When the time comes, they'll just use past results to mock other games again, which I find quite 'delightful'.

top.en: Did you watch big bro's [~0:Chovy] first game? That's what you call flashing and opening with R right into their faces, desperately forcing plays and creating opportunities out of nothing to maximize an assassin's advantage, and that was even from an even game state! What about Knight? Seemingly starts 3/0, but what happens? Hesitant, cowardly, playing teamfights with the absolute safest textbook formula: first throw out E, if E connects, fly in, drop W, get hit by random AOE and knockups, beaten to a pulp, and then start panicking and looking for an escape route. His playstyle always picks the safest, most conservative, [~1:cowardly] option, only ever playing inside his comfort zone. The moment he faces any pressure, stress, or a game state beyond his expectations, he loses his mind, completely blanks out, gets dumbfounded, and starts planning his getaway. It's genuinely unreal. In my memory, if he gets ten 2/0, 3/0, or 4/0 starts, somehow the game always ends up even. This happens way too much—most of the time he can only play when ahead, acting all cocky. And another thing: in 1v1s or small skirmishes, you clearly look comfortable, but the moment a big teamfight breaks out and the enemy groups up, his true colors show. It's masterclass hesitation; he's completely stumped, has no idea what to do, and can only fight when outnumbering the enemy. The second there are too many people, his poor little heart can't handle it and he completely forgets how to play. When you're behind, having a lead earlier makes zero difference, your impact on the game is totally average. And another thing that shows just how conservative and cowardly your playstyle is: in your memory, your Flash is always used for escaping, and even then you still end up dying last because you panicked over low health. You're never decisive on the offense—you hesitate, hold your Flash until there's no chance left, finally think about using it to run, and get chased down and slapped to death. Offensive Flashes and playmaking Flashes are practically nonexistent unless it's a smurfing game where the outcome is already in the bag. Why on earth does someone with such amazing mechanical talent have such a spineless, coward's personality? It's absolute waste of raw talent. Personality truly determines destiny. If you just had a slightly bigger heart, were braver, more proactive, dared to actively make and create plays, and snatched openings from the jaws of defeat, your career honors and public reputation would undoubtedly be way beyond what they are now. Sigh, it's genuinely pathetic. Cowardice and conservatism are etched into your very core, nothing can be done about it. What a damn shame.
